keyframe_review.note: 36,109 km2, bbox 13.03-18.44 E, 39.90-43.60 N: from Asculum and the Marsi to the Sallentine peninsula, one blob for both theatres. Fits the page's theatres ('the northern theatre was centred on Asculum, in the lands of the Piceni and Marsi'; 'The southern theatre covered Samnium, Lucania, Apulia, and Campania') and its loyal exceptions: 'Rome also kept control of Capua and central Campania' and 'Rome's Latin allies remained loyal' (the Latin colonies inside the blob are not drawn separately). Shortened to 90: the northern theatre collapsed in 89.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the lex Julia (October 90) and the fall of Asculum (November 89) 'the insurgents fled to the south, where the Italians still controlled large tracts of territory'; Sulla took Pompeii and Bovianum in 89. The southern theatre only.

region.text: the rebel allies' lands from Picenum to Lucania, without Roman Capua and Naples

ledger.note: 91 BC: the Italian confederation. 'The war began in late 91 BC with the rebellion of Asculum'; the Italians 'set up a capital at Corfinium with a forum and a five-hundred-man senate', with Quintus Poppaedius Silo (north) and Gaius Papius Mutilus (south) as consuls. Belligerents: the Marsic group (Marsi, Paeligni, Vestini, Marrucini, Picentes, Frentani) and the Samnite group (Samnites, Campanians, Iapygians, Lucanians, Hirpini, Venusia). The name 'Italia' 'appears only in Mommsen's interpretation'.

91-87 BC: the Social War. 'The war began in late 91 BC with the rebellion of Asculum'; Marius 'inflicted a defeat on the Marsi near the Fucine Lake' in 90 BC, after the Tolenus River battle of 11 June 90 BC. [Reviewer eu-03-c, 2026-10-19: quote corrected: the page dates the Tolenus battle and Marius' Fucine Lake victory to 90 BC, not 91]

89 BC: 'Corfinium was also taken, forcing the Italians to transfer their capital to Bovianum.' The page gives no explicit year; the sentence sits in its 89 BC narrative (after 'The new consuls for 89 BC were Gnaeus Pompeius Strabo and Lucius Porcius Cato'). [Reviewer eu-03-c, 2026-10-19: moved from 90 to 89 and confidence 3 to 2, per the page's 89 BC narrative]
89 BC: Bovianum 'was later taken by Sulla in 89 BC, and the capital moved to Aesernia'.

minus.text: the northern theatre: Asculum, the Marsi, Paeligni, Vestini, Marrucini, Picentes and Frentani

region.text: the Marsi, Paeligni, Vestini, Marrucini and Frentani country, Asculum excepted

ledger.note: 90 BC: the lex Julia, 'decreed around October 90 BC', 'granted citizenship to Italian communities that had not revolted or promptly laid down arms'; Marius' and Pompeius Strabo's campaigns in the north. Drawn as the loss of the Marsic lands apart from Asculum over the winter of 90/89 (the page: the northern theatre collapsed after Asculum). [Reviewer eu-03-c, 2026-10-19: moved from October 90 to summer 89: the page says the northern front 'largely collapsed' after the 90 victories, but in 89 the Romans 'forced the Marsi to petition for peace', 'also subjugated the Vestini and the Marrucini' and took Corfinium, and 'By summer, the Romans had pacified the northern theatre, except for Asculum']
89 BC: Asculum 'Surrendered in November 89 BC after its commander Vidacilius committed suicide'; the northern theatre ends.

region.text: rebel Campania around Pompeii and Nuceria, Nola excepted

ledger.note: 89 BC: Campania. Pompeii 'Taken by Sulla in 89 BC'; Sulla 'besieged Nola in 89 BC, and was still besieging it when he marched on Rome in 88 BC'. Campania (less Nola) returns to Rome; Bovianum falls the same year.
88 BC: Apulia. Silo 'Killed in 88 BC in Apulia, after his forces were defeated by Quintus Caecilius Metellus Pius'.

region.text: Samnium and Lucania, the last rebel country

ledger.note: 87 BC: 'the Samnites and Lucanians were nominally pacified in 87 BC' through 'a negotiated settlement during the civil war of 87 BC, when they sided with Cinna and Marius'; the lex Plautia Papiria (89) had 'excluded the Samnites and Lucanians, who were still under arms'. 'A remnant held out in Bruttium' and 'an identifiably Italian group of rebels was at last defeated' only at the Colline Gate (November 82), which is the Roman civil war, not this state.

region.text: Samnium and Lucania, the last rebel country

ledger.note: 87 BC: the confederation dissolves into Roman citizen communities; Nola's holdouts and the Samnite remnant of 82 are noted, not drawn.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Italian City-States' row (-91..-88, one 36,109 km2 shape) is mislabelled: its Wikipedia article 'Italian city-states' is about the medieval and Renaissance communes and 'none of these' (Social War, Italia, Corfinium) 'is mentioned in the text'; the seed's wikidata Q4115680 is that medieval article's and is kept only because no better id could be checked (wikidata.org is unreachable). The row is the Italian allies' confederation of the Social War, so identity.wikipedia is set to 'Social War (91–87 BC)', the type to rebel (rule 5) and the name to 'Italia' with the page's caution that the name 'appears only in Mommsen's interpretation'. Start 91 (month 11, 'late 91 BC'); end moved from 88 to 87 (infobox '91-87 BC'; Samnites and Lucanians 'nominally pacified in 87 BC'). The single shape is right for 91-90 less Roman Capua, central Campania and Naples; two new keyframes narrow it to the southern theatre (89) and to Samnium-Lucania (88-87). Capitals Corfinium -> Bovianum (90) -> Aesernia (89). Counterpart throughout: roman-republic, whose dossier mirrors these events (loss 91, gains 89-87).
